newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific sees small value in Amoco sale.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific sees small value in Amoco sale.

text.p: Union Pacific Resources Group Inc is on the hunt for acquisitions but does not see great value in the $2.0 to $2.5 billion of properties being auctioned by Amoco Corp.

"It is no secret that we have a whole team of people working on acquisitions, it is just that at first blush there does not appear to be a great deal of value in the properties Amoco is selling," said a spokesman for Union Pacific.
Amoco announced last week that it would sell 15 percent of its U.S. reserves, mostly natural gas producing properties in Wyoming, Colorado, New Mexico and the Gulf Coast.
The cost of producing energy from the properties to be sold is some $4.40 per barrel of oil equivalent, compared with an average across all of Amoco of $3.70.
"We are looking for a big acquisition and we have the cash to finance it, but this is probably not the deal," said the Union Pacific spokesman.

Union Pacific chief operating officer George Lindahl told a conference in New York recently that the company, which is the largest energy independent in the U.S., could borrow up to $3.0 billion and still maintain its "A" credit rating.
Apache Corp and Burlington Resources Inc have indicated that they are interested in some of the properties.
